text:
maya: Hey team — proposing we intake a new candidate model 'Velvet-7B-v2' for evaluation. Quick heads-up: the published weights come with a 'NonCommercial-ShareAlike 1.0' header and an attribution addendum. Can legal confirm whether that blocks hosting on our Redwood API?

sam (legal): @maya thanks for flagging. NC = non-commercial; hosting a paid/shared API is almost always considered commercial. We need to see the exact license text and any downstream addendums. Link? :mag_right:

maya: pasted excerpt below (from the GitHub release):

```
Copyright 2025 VelvetAI
This model is licensed under NonCommercial-ShareAlike 1.0 (NC-SA-1.0).
You must provide attribution and may not use the model for commercial purposes without permission.
```

maya: full release notes: https://github.com/velvetai/velvet-7b/releases/tag/v2.0

license-bot: Automated license scan results: Velvet-7B-v2 -> NC-SA-1.0 (HIGH-RISK). Contains training provenance notes referencing datasets with third-party restrictions. Recommend manual legal review.

toni: fwiw, we ran a quick int8/4-bit quant test on a local infra fork — perf is great, perplexity delta ~+2.2% vs fp16. But we also saw some safety-regression on misinformation prompts in the eval bench. Not huge, but notable.

liam: Product note — we have a pilot customer asking for a hosted endpoint for internal summaries; they'd be paying. If NC applies, we can't offer hosted. Dedicated or private tenancy might be possible if the license allows on-prem non-commercial, but likely still an issue.

sam (legal): Short answer: can't list it in hosted catalog or provide as part of our hosted multi-tenant API unless we get an explicit commercial license from VelvetAI. For Dedicated we need to inspect the license wording about "distribution" and "use by third parties" — many NC licenses still preclude customer-paid services. Private (customer-managed) deployments are a different bucket but still need provenance and indemnities.

maya: OK — proposal: 1) mark Velvet-7B-v2 as NO_HOSTED in intake dashboard, 2) do a private/dedicated permissibility check for a specific customer (if they sign a commercial license or we broker one), 3) run a provenance & dataset-usage deep-dive, 4) block for public benchmarks until cleared. Thoughts?

sam (legal): Agreed. Action items for legal: open LEGAL-1264 to request clarification from VelvetAI and to seek a commercial license option. Also run a copyright provenance check on the checkpoints (who uploaded, commit history).

toni: Action items for eng-ml: add Velvet-7B-v2 to the regression watchlist, attach quantization logs and our safety eval run (tiny sample). I'll drop the eval JSON into the intake ticket. :white_check_mark:

liam: Product: I'll flag the customer and ask whether they can accept a self-hosted/private deployment. If they insist on hosted, we'll decline until license is cleared.

maya: Quick checklist I'm putting on the intake record (feel free to copy):
- license type identified (NC-SA)
- hosted permissibility: NO (pending exception)
- Dedicated permissibility: PENDING (legal review)
- Private deployment: MAYBE (depends on upstream terms + SSO/KMS)
- provenance / uploader verification: TODO
- quantization tests ran: YES (int8, int4) -> perf ok, small quality delta
- safety regressions: YES (small) -> attach eval set
- request commercial license from upstream: TODO (LEGAL-1264)

sam (legal): Add a checklist item: confirm training dataset licenses (some datasets referenced look like "non-redistributable" or have API-use restrictions). If any training data restricts commercial derivative use, that complicates everything.

license-bot: Note: VelvetAI repo includes third-party dataset notice -> "DSET-X: redistribution restricted". Flagged file: datasets/README.md

maya: Can someone from infra help capture a canonical snapshot of the exact artifact (checksum, commit, release tarball) so legal can reference it? I don't want someone to re-upload a slightly different file later.

toni: I'll grab sha256 and store in the intake ticket. Command I used:

```
sha256sum velvet-7b-v2.ckpt
# -> 4f2a9c... (saved to intake/velvet7b-v2/sha256.txt)
```

sam (legal): Good. Also capture the upstream contact (maintainer email) and date of release. We'll email them for a dual-license request. Template: short ask, commercial terms, and whether dataset contributors allow relicensing.

liam: One more product nuance — we often allow customers to bring their own model (BYOM) into Dedicated. If someone wants to run Velvet-7B-v2 on Dedicated with customer-provided keys/artifacts, is that still allowed? Sam?

sam (legal): BYOM where customer supplies the model artifact and hosts it completely in their environment is usually OK, but we need to ensure we do not distribute or materially modify the model. If we touch the weights or host it on our infra for them, that crosses into distribution/service. We'll add a BYOM decision tree to LEGAL-1264.

maya: Thanks. I'll update the intake record with NO_HOSTED status and link LEGAL-1264 and the sha file.

sam (legal): Final note: there are 3 routes forward: 1) upstream grants commercial/dual license (preferred), 2) get indemnity / special terms for enterprise (possible but slow), 3) choose a different model with permissive license. Recommend option 1 or 3 for speed.

maya: Cool. Everyone: please drop any additional logs/links into the intake ticket. I'll ping again after legal updates. :thumbsup:
